input: The memo recommends a three-month pilot of maintenance sensors before any decision on full installation. The pilot covers 24 pumps at a cost of $39k. The reliability engineering group owns the pilot and reports before the March capital review; the decision on full installation is held until the pilot results are reported. The plant runs 260 pumps. Maintenance records for 12 months show 1177 h of unplanned downtime, and bearing failures account for 40% of the downtime hours. A sensor set for all 260 pumps is quoted at $423k installed, plus $58k per year. In a vendor trial on a comparable unit, the sensors cut downtime by 27%; the figure is a vendor figure and was not measured at this plant. Spare-part lead times are unchanged by the sensors. The trade-off stands in one comparison: $39k buys a plant measurement, while $423k plus $58k per year commits the plant on a vendor figure. The pilot is read on the plant's own maintenance records, so its result and the baseline share a basis. Until the pilot reports, the plant's position is unchanged: the downtime stands on the record, and no installation is committed. The full-installation decision follows the pilot report at the March capital review.
